title: Typological Study On the Workplace Faith Fellowship In Its Three Stages of Historical Development in Korea
abstract: I. INTRODUCTION A. Posing of Problem and the Task of Study The National Statistical Office reported that about 22,219,000 workers are employed nationwide by the September, 2002. This numeric reaches 46.6% of the whole population in Korea. Recent report says that workers feel discouraged and unsecured because of the hostile working environment, limitless competition, structural injustice of industrial society, economic and societal conflict between the rich and the poor, psychological stress and tension, collapse of family and virtue system, and, blurring of the ethical sensitivity in the workplace. It is not surprising therefore to hear from the groups of age in 20' and 30' complaining of their unstable job and future. 'For where two or three are gathered together in my name, I am there in the midst of them' (Mt. 18:20). So many believers have experienced hope and consolation from this text. The text gives not only psychological easiness but also Chris tian vision of vocation that the workplace is the one in which Christ's presence is to be experienced and witnessed. Workplace Faith Fellowship has been the place in which believers are exposed to the concrete real world and encouraged to create and participate in the mystical visible body of Christ, and called to share Christian life in a hostile real world of selfishness, competition, and injustice. It has challenged believers to live with honesty and responsibility the wholistic Christian life supposed to be accomplished through the interconnected structures of family, church, and work place. Considering of its original vision, however, future of the WF appears to be not so hopeful because of the accelerating process of secularization in society. For the writer devoting to the workplace ministry in the Holy Love Church Furniture Company last ten years, current situation is discouraging. How could I revitalize and realize the original vision of the workplace mission? How could I form the faith community in workplace in which believers are challenged to express and create their Christian identity? How could believers be more faithful to Christ's simple words like these: 'Go into all the world and preach the gospel to every creature' (Mark 16:15); 'You are the salt of the earth but if the salt loses its flavor, how shall it be seasoned? It is then good for nothing but to be thrown out and trampled underfoot by men' (Matthew 5:13). Task of the study is to characterize and evaluate the activities and influence of WFs by using four typologies the writer creates, that is, the worship-centered, the Bible study-centered, the mission-centered, and fellowship-centered, from theological and sociological perspectives, with its three stages of historical development in view. Motif of the study is to help members, leaders, prospective leaders of WF and church leadership confronting ones' history and thereby revitalizing their self-identity in a new way. B. Methodology and the Scope of the Study The study depends on literary analysis of diverse materials from WF and visitation. In Introduction, task and motif of the study will be revealed. Scope of study will be defined. In Chapter II, theoretical ground of WF will be laid, historically, theologically, and sociologically. Historical origins of three categories of WF especially in connection with its leadership style be introduced historically. Theological principles or assumptions of WF will be analyzed in terms of the nature of laity, stewardship, and mission of sending. In sociological analysis, the writer will deal with the value of vocation in diverse perspectives. Chapter III, IV and V deal with history of the WF in its three stages of development: the early (1950'-1970'), the middle (1980'-1990'), and the present (2000-present). Activities in each stage will be explored and characterized in four typologies: the worship centered, the Bible study centered, the mission centered, and the fellowship-diakonia centered, evaluated from theological and sociological perspective, and, summarized critically. II. Theoretical Reflection on Workplace Faith Fellowship A. Historical Reflection The writer analyzes the history of Korean WF in four typologies of the worship centered, the Bible Study Centered, mission centered, and fellowship centered. Four typologies are categorized in terms of the primary concerns and focuses of activities of diverse groups of WF. Though not adopted as a categorizing typology in the thesis, another perspective to categorize WFs would be worth being remarked. It is related to the question of leadership, that is, 'who takes initiative to run WF. 1. Independent Workplace Faith Fellowship Historical origin of WF is known to be a prayer meeting held in Dansung Sa (movie theater) run at that time by Byuksan Co. in 1956. Initiative of this meeting was taken by a devote Christian owner of Byuksan Co.. Theater was open to public on Sunday. And Christians of employees in the company couldn't attend Sunday Worship Service. The owner felt deeply sorry about this situation, finally decided to provide certain space and time (one of weekday) for employees to have opportunity to have service. Though not systematically organized and given space for more creative and extended activities compared to WF today, WF in Dansung Sa is a historical phenomena in Korean christian soil in which worship service celebrated in the church on Sunday is the normative considered biblical and therefore effective. Characteristic of this type of WF is that the owner of the company takes initiative and the activities are restricted more or less within that company. 2. Workplace Mission Association In the pluralistic secular city like Seoul, there are so many big companies, officially not affiliated to any religion. It is hard in this case to get any help for Christian activities from companies, for example. Under this circumstance, there comes up individual Christians, forming an areal christian network which could be called WF. Usually they ask churches in area to provide space and sometimes leadership for meeting. The meeting held at Chonkyo Methodist Church in 1979 is the one in this kind. They first called the meeting as 'Thursday workplace church' because they met at Thursday lunchtime. Members of this meeting introduced their activities around the area, invited other Christian workers to the Easter Service in 1980, and decided to develop 'Thursday workplace church' into 'Workplace Mission Association.' This type of WF has been established since then in big cities, now reaching the nationwide networking of 38 areal organizations by now. In this type of WF, leadership or the initiative is taken by christian workers' network voluntarily established, but with strong relationship with one church in the area who provides meeting space, financial support, and some part of leadership. 3. Workplace Church Worship Workplace Church Worship is a type of meeting in which a certain church takes full initiative in making organization, funding, and providing leadership. The meeting usually origins as a result of mission project of an urban church for the area. Youngrak Presbyterian church began this type of mission project September 5 1969. Church invited workers of Ssang Yong Cement, Bbaek general hospital, Jungbu police station and began worship service at lunch time every Friday. In this type of WP, leadership is under a local church. B. Theological Reflection 1. Theology of Laity Theological ground of WF appears to be theology of laity which is based on the doctrine of priesthood of believers reclaimed by Martin Luther. Luther argued that the only mediator is Jesus Christ and christians baptized have grace of privilege to participate in Christ's priesthood as his visible body in this world. This means that every christian has a duty and privilege to proclaim gospel and offer a prayer of intercession in every place and time, offering spiritual and living worship. Priesthood and apostolic right is not just restricted to the church institution (ordained clergy). Priesthood is to be reinterpreted and applied to all believers in Jesus Christ. The doctrine of priesthood of believers is the ground of the theology of laity and theological justification of WF. What is the biblical meaning of the term 'laity'? As 'laos,' in Greek, it indicates people of God including both clergy and believers not ordained. The term 'laity' is a glorious word because people of God is nothing other than a chosen race, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, God's own people made to proclaim the mighty acts of him who call themselves out of darkness into his marvelous light (1 Peter 2:9). In the early stage of the Christian history, laity means community of believers including apostles, prophets, teachers, deacons, and others given diverse gifts from Holy Spirit, only later, coming to be degraded when it began to indicate a group of believers unordained, passive, derivative and secondary compared to the ordained in the mission of the church. Theology of laity based upon the doctrine of priesthood of believers appears to be implied or assumed in activities of WF. 2. Theology of Stewardship Another theological principle of workplace mission comes from Genesis 1: 28: 'have dominion over the fish of the sea and over the bird....' Message is about stewardship assigned and commanded to human being as image of God. Steward is the faithful and prudent manager (Luke 12:42), servants of Christ and steward of God's mysteries (1 Cor. 4:1), guardians and trustees, blameless (Gal. 4:2). To serve the world as Christ did is one of theological principles which could explain WF's activities in meaningful way. 3. Theology of 'Being Sent' Jesus Christ trained his disciples for three years, sending them to the world. In John 17:18 reading 'As you have sent me into the world, so I have sent them onto the world,' what we see is the special relationship among God, Jesus Christ and disciples, the relationship characterized as 'sending' and 'sent.' God sent Jesus and Jesus sent disciples. Message is about mission and the importance of the relation between the one who send and the one who is sent. Sender gives full authority to the one who is sent. The one to be sent represents the sender in full scale. Jesus also commands to his disciples just before ascension: 'Go therefore and make disciples of all nations' (Mt. 28:19). This command of mission is passed over to members of WF through the disciples. WF is community to be sent to make disciples by God in and through Jesus Christ in this world, that is, in workplace. Being sent is an important theological perspective to have members of WF see their vocation with responsibility and faith. C. Sociological Reflection Korean war (1950-1953) had devastated Korean economy. Poverty was the main issue and problem to be solved to any subsequent political leaderships thereafter. Since 1962 Korean government launched a grand project called '5 Year Economic Development Plan.' The first '5 Year Economic Development Plan' was accomplished during 1962-1966 and the fifth and the last one during 1977-1981. 25 years of national project to elevate economic standard brought rapid and dramatic economic development and prosperity on the one hand, however, moral hazard and loss of ethics of work on the other hand resulting in the IMF period (1997-19998). WF understands their workplace as a mission field and vocation as place in and through which one is called to the service of God and the world. This kind of highly ethical and theological perception of vocation in the consciousness of members of WF came to be known and valued in and out of WF in this one-dimensional wasteland of this kingdom of profit. III. The Initial Stage of Workplace Faith Fellowship (1950s-1980s) A. Worship Centered Workplace Faith Fellowship 1. National Assembly Prayer Breakfast National Assembly Prayer Breakfast was begun in November 1965 by Christian members of the 6th National Assembly, led by Assemblywoman Hyun-Sook Park. The meeting was begun to better love brothers and sisters in Christ, to worship, and was started with the prayer that 'His will be done' in our nation 'as in Heaven.' In May of 1968, the National Assembly Prayer Breakfast and the Korean Prayer Breakfast Committees jointly established National Prayer Breakfast, an annual event where the President, prominent figures of the three departments of the government, and other leaders of different spheres of influence, gathered to pray. Those attending this Prayer Breakfast, despite their unique positions as members of the Assembly, approached the workplace with a firm sense of Christian duty, and the event sublimated into one in which true workplace worship occurred. Their main activity was their Prayer Breakfasts that were held on the first Wednesdays of each month at 7:30 am in the National Assembly Prayer Room (13206), during which the members held service and shared breakfast. They also held service on the days regular as well as extraordinary Assembly meetings were called to order. What is specially noteworthy is that even after the Christian members of the Assembly in opposing parties had confronted each other in fierce debates, they would always worship as one in Christ, giving honor to God and sharing love in fellowship with one another. 2. National Assembly Prayer Meetings National Assembly Prayer Meetings are a separate WF from National Assembly Breakfast Prayer. This WF had its start when three sisters in Christ (Kyung-Hae Kim, Young-Sook Choi, Chi-Myung Park) met to hold a prayer meeting on October 22, 1976. At the time, with no rooms available in which to have worship, the group of three met in storage rooms, ventilation room, or utility rooms to raise up earnest, tearful prayers. By God's provision they were able to hold their first meeting in their newly obtained permanent prayer room, in basement room 206, on September 12, 1979. The sound of prayer never ceased coming from this room for an entire year. On December 26 1979, the National Assembly Prayer Association's Inaugural General Synod (President: Chang-Lyul Kim) met, and on January 5th 1980 they held an Inaugural Worship Service Sermon: Bishop Gi-Chun Jang). B. Bible Study Centered Workplace Faith Fellowship As Bible study centered WF, Faith Movement for Bankers of the Bank of Korea can be pick up. It had its humble beginnings on August 27, 1975 with three people at the preparatory prayer meeting. On November 26 the same year, they had the Inaugural General Synod and began its growth as a WF. The regulation established at this time, 'We are to spread Biblically grounded Gospel, and in fostering interrelationship among members, give glory to God,' was the purpose of this ministry and now, 20 years after, the same holds. From March 20, 1978 four teams of 40 members committed to group Bible studies began. For those who may wonder, 'Why Bible studies at this particular time?', it could be said that the studies were prompted by the 'New Living' seminar that was started at Bank of We. At the time in 1978, over the course of four days of February 14th to the 17th at the 2nd meeting, an average of 350 people attended every day, making the Bank of Korea auditorium a place where many were touched. As an outflow of such memorable experience Bible study groups sprang up in different departments. As teaching material they used what Pastor Dong-Won Lee (Then Faith Movement for Bankers leader and Pastor of Global Missions Church) provided, 'The 9 Steps of the Creed.' The Bible studies span on average 30 to 40 minutes, and are divided into times of Bible study, prayer, fellowship, and praise. About 80% of the time is spent on the study of the Bible, which is also divided into Bible reading, teaching, and sharing, of which teaching is alloted 50% of the time. Outside the regular meetings, the Bible study members meet to visit and serve at centers for the disabled and senior citizens. They also collect money to celebrate special occasions such as birthdays and promotions, to give farewell gifts to those being transferred, and in addition, many groups jointly go on one day prayer retreats. C. Mission Centered Workplace Faith Fellowship The Missions Society of Seoul Bank is WF that was founded in the midst of much discord and hurt resulting from the merger between Seoul Bank and Sintak Bank in 1976. The group had its beginning as a seemingly inconsiderable prayer meeting. It was Jong-Bok Kim, then central staff member of CCC (Korea Campus Crusade for Christ)6), who had vision of having a group 'Centered ministering lay people at the workplace,' and to help foster the 'growth as a global bank' in order to 'share in the vision of world missions' which made the birth of this group, on January 1977, possible. In September of 1997, this small society grew to include 500 registered members with chapters in Busan, Jam-sil Jun-San Center, L.A., and developed to have different departments specializing in worship Service, evangelism, volunteering, pamphlet missions, and musical praise. To vitalize the regional chapters, advising pastors and/or officers are appointed to go and to take part in their worship services, partake in fellowship, and exchange information, particularly in order to discuss evangelism methods. Those from the main headquarters regularly attend meetings at the chapters and are jointly pushing for business missions. D. Fellowship-Diakonia Centered Workplace Faith Fellowship 1. Investment Firms Workplace Faith Fellowship At the starting point of the history of Korean WF, we find the Investment firm WF. On December 27; 1977, Christian employees working in investment firms with a united desire to spread the Gospel in their field established three independent WFs in the old National Theatre in Myoung Dong. The mission statement of the group was to foster the holy fellowship of believers in the realm of investment and to accomplish Jesus Christ's great missions commission. As they remained true to these founding principles and put them to action, the group now consists of 30 investment firms WFs with 3000 members spread over the country, including their four regional chapters in Busan, Gwang Joo, Ool San, and Dae Gu, and becomes an influential missions organization. 2. Youngrak Church's Workplace Church Worship Different from unit WFs with leadership taken by a particular WF and meeting held during the weekday, for workplace church worship type of WF, leadership is provided by the local church. This local church provides with leadership, fund, meeting place and other ones in need. This is immediately related to city church's mission strategy to reaching out surrounding regional community. This WP started by Youngnak Church (Senior Pastor: Chul-Shin Lee) located in Ju-Dong, Seoul, and also that first of its kind in Korea, celebrates its 35th anniversary in 2004. During lunch break of yet another ordinary Friday September 5th 1969, this kind of WF was offered to the workers in the area who were employed at places such as Ssang Young Cement, Bbaek General Hospital, and the Junbu Police Station. 10 people had attended the first worship service but at the present some 200 people have become regulars. E. Evaluation 1. Sociological and Theological Evaluation The economic state of Korea in its beginnings as a modern country was dismal. After the tragedy of the fratricidal Korean War, country faces a great hardship. Factories, buildings, railroads, and other facilities of value were all destroyed, and the toll on human life was tremendous. According to data from an organization, civilian casualties soared as high as 244, 663 for South Korea alone, higher for North Korea with 406,000 dead, with 303,212 missing, and 680,000 wounded or injured. No doubt, it was a period of great darkness. Notwithstanding, WF that was started in 1956 sublimated the deep hurts from the war with faith, and took on the great task of spreading the Gospel, and of serving society. When giving a theological (ecclesiological) evaluation of the WF in its early years, one should make it from the theological perspective of 'sending.' God is the subject of missions. God's mission began with the sending of His son Jesus Christ into this world, and the love that sent His only son was not limited to Israel or a certain nation but was meant for all of humanity. The theological perspective of 'sending' characterizes the nature of activities of WF in its initial stage of historical development. Also thanks to this theology the worship, service format centered on the leadership of minister gave way to that grounded upon the leadership of laity. This theology justifies the fact that worship could be brought out from the church building into the outside world. 2. Overall Evaluation It is worth noting that WF in its early stage was established out of the poor lay leaderships, inferior working environment in which general ethos is so opposite from that of Christian vision of living, and absence of more or less articulated theological ground. Namely, it would be likely that the most active minority are not in the mainstream in the workplace. This would probably result in WF's somewhat restricted influence on workplace or the society. Attempting to classify the various WFs from the early years, the writer suffers most because of rarity of materials answering questions like these: 'How many leaders were working?' 'how were they equipped with more technical knowledge,' 'how were new comers trained and nurtured?' 'how many people worked actively?' IV. The Middle Stage of the Workplace Faith Fellowship (1981-1990) A. Worship Centered Workplace Faith Fellowship 1. Sung-Ae Church Furniture Company Sung-Ae Church Furniture Company was founded on 1967. Company motto was 'Safely and Faithfully,' 'Diligently and Wisely,' 'Enduring Faith.' The company places priority on WF worship. In 1977, after the Sung-Ae Furniture Company Factory was rebuilt for expansion, Thanksgiving Service (sermon: Pastor Jung-Soo Park) was held. From this worship, the company's WF worship was decided to take on a new form as 'Monday Service,' with the purpose of offering the first hour of the workweek to God. Of course, there have been services at Sung-Ae from its founding, but it was in a form that merely followed class meeting order of Methodist Church. Main Activities focused on missions in and abroad, miscellaneous activities, which would actualize philosophy of management: 'Glory to God. 2. Ebenezer of Samsung Electronics Ebenezer is the name of WF in Samsung Electronics, an affiliated enterprise of Samsung Group, located in Gi-Heung of Kyoung-Gi Provence. It started when Chul Jin Lee (at present Professor of Nano Technology at Han Yang University), Kwang-Hee Yang, and a few other brothers met to hold worship services together in 1984. Main activities of this WF is as follow: regular meetings (Tuesdays every week at the women's dormitory Baek-Hap dong education center in basement, 6pm); prayer meetings at Paul Prayer Center; missions abroad Ebenezer retreat. 3. Christian Workplace Faith Fellowship of Seoul Subway Corporation The Christian WF of Seoul Subway Corporation held its initiation meeting on June 29, 1984, and held the Christian WF worship commemorating its founding September 15, 1984. They named the community as 'Christian WF of Seoul Subway Corporation,' and elected Han Mo Jung as president, and, celebrated its inaugural worship servide with Rev. Yong Gi Cho (Yoido Full Gospel Church) as speaker on October 6th 1984. Jae Myung Kim (CEO) and other 500 people were present. They opened a sanctuary in Sin Chun Station (subway line 2) on October 20, and began its WF activities. Main Activities are as follow: regular monthly services; inaugural worship wervice; Christmas Tree Lighting worship service; relief services; funding missionaries abroad and/or Church Planting efforts; funding concert choir; coalition report publication; spreading Gospel at workplace; funding workplace mission general assemblies; managing and running sanctuary and offices. B. Bible Study Centered Workplace Faith Fellowship 1. Business Bible Belt ('BBB') BBB had its beginning when around 40 workers in Myong Dong business area gathered together to study the Bible on January of 1990, to be trained and nurtured in faith, and to accomplish discipleship fully and effectively in workplace given to them. This has become an extensive organization. This WF has 1,300 participating members in cities of Seoul (areas of Myoung Dong, Gwang Hwa Moon, Seoul Station, Gang Nam, Yoido) and is active in other cities like Chun An, Dae Gu, Dae Jun, Ik San. It is interesting to note that this WF has its chapter even in Singapore. BBB's strategy for mission is as follow: living out a life of evangelism in the workplace; establishing a small size of groups of Bible study; cultivating leadership; working together for spreading the Gospel. C. Mission Centered Workplace Faith Fellowship 1. Workplace Faith Fellowship Federation of Incheon: WF Federation of Incheon was established May 5, 1988, with following objectives: sanctification of Incheon through strengthening relations among various WF groups, and through vitalizing workplace ministries fostering a Christian culture in the Incheon workplace and its society through individual WF's attempt to elevate quality of educational service activities, vitalize the Christian spirituality helping members living out of faith having unification of WFs movements as the group's main concerns putting to action the slogan such as 'Offer Incheon to God! Sanctification of Incheon through workplace mission! Glory to God by faith and missions!';spreading the Gospel in the workplace by the joining of 100 individual WFs; funding and commissioning missionaries abroad. 2. Workplace Faith Fellowship Federation of the City of Yuh Soo: WT Federation of the city of Yuh Soo, at first emerging as an ecumenical laity movement, was established in its present form on January 12, 1984 with Soon Ahn Kim as its first president. Now it numbers 1500 in 28 WFs. Its slogan is 'Workplace Missions! Evangelize the Region! Glory to God!' with practical objectives such as: evangelization of the region through vitalization of workplace mission; creation of Christian spirituality in workplace by living out the Christian spirituality; unity of Church by the strengthening of interrelations within WFs. 3. Workplace Faith Fellowship Federation of Kyoung Buk and the city of Dae Gu. On March 3, 1990, a planning committee of 11 members for the founding of WF federation of Kyung Buk and the city of Dae Gu was formed with having Inaugural General Assembly started at Don Il Church on May 19, 1990. This WF federation includes Korean Electric WF as well as thirteen other WFs. Main activities are as follow: opening of Misba Public Square Special Testimony; providing Bible studies for workers; publishing and distributing evangelistic reading material for the purpose of spreading the Gospel in the workplace; making evangelistic publications to indict idolatry culture in Dae-Gu Kyung-Buk. 4. Workplace Faith Fellowship Federation of the city of Chun Chun Founded on April 17 1990 at Dong Bu Presbyterian Chruch by the elder Gwang Olng Huh, this WF federation's main activities are as follow: monthly worship services; annual fund raising event; holding of regular prayer meetings; evangelism meetings--roadside evangelism, evangelism in event halls, joint assemblies with the Choon-Chun Christian coalition; weekly Thursday prayer meetings for the sanctification of the city of Choon-Chun; publication of Choon Chun City Sanctification Newsletter; training members at Intercession Prayer Schools. 5. Workplace Faith Fellowship of Ul-Jin Nuclear Power Station Ul-Jin Nuclear Power Station WF was founded in the fall of 1985, with the conviction that Christians, based on II Corinthians 2:14, must be the fragrance of the knowledge of Christ in the workplace. They hold regular worship services every Thursday (12:00-12:30pm) in the Library of the 1st floor of Welfare Facilities Building, and also have Praise Services every Monday (12:00-12:30pm) in the same location. Main Activities are as follow: funding of CCC staff member Sung-Jin Kim; funding of the Hallelujah Boys Youth Soccer Club of Ul-Jin; missions through Han-Jun Power Company Group. This WF also funds three missionaries in Pakistan, Laos, and France as a supporting project for missions abroad. Besides these activities it involved in relief work and local church events. D. Fellowship-Diakonia Centered Workplace Faith Fellowship 1. The United Korea Energies Workplace Faith Fellowship 'Heralds of Light, triumph over the darkness' (Korean hymnal. 259). Every year on July 1, on the founding day of the company (and thus a company holiday), all the Christian WFs of the Korea Electric Power Corporation scattered all over the country gather together with one heart and sing this hymn with all their might. On the day of the National Federation Meeting Han-Nam University in the city of Dae Jun, there was an urgent motion to initiate missionary work by giving up lunch for a month for the Lord. Immediately members of WFs from all over the nation were invited to join in the vision and to facilitate an efficient management of ministries. For the task, WFs of different regions, a National Federation of WF and WF association were established and officers elected. To start with, each WF voluntarily collected monetary offerings in order to assist agencies going through hardships in the neighboring areas, to help needy families, and to aid other coagent missionary groups. A part of the collected funds are sent to provincial WF association and/or the National Federation of WF to expand their ministries in a national level. 2. Korea Drivers Mission Association On December 16, 1981 the Korea Drivers Mission Society was founded, and on April 16, 1985 their office moved to the Road Traffic Safety Association. At the first regular general assembly by electing deacon Bu Ha Yoo as its first president and Sung Sook Yoo as business secretary, the Korea Drivers Mission Association officially began. Main activities are as follow: preaching the Gospel to drivers (Evangelism through each company, restaurants for drivers, and Model Drivers Association); evangelism of passengers via distribution of evangelic publications; broadcasting ministries (recommending listening to the Christian Broadcasting Station, and Far-East Broadcasting Station); having praise and sermon tapes ready in the vehicle to allow passengers to listen; hold Evangelical Praise Competitions. E. Evaluation 1 Sociological and Theological Evaluation It would not be a stretch to say that phenomenal flourishing of Korea WFs in this middle period was a beneficiary of the impressive economic growth of the 1980s and 90s. After the Korean War, government adopted forceful economic policies, and accomplished amazing task which could be called 'the miracle of Han River.' Korea has been changed drastically from the agricultural nation to the highly developed industrial nation in this period. 2. General Evaluation WFs in this period were under the situation of astounding economic growth and development. It is to be noted, however, that economic growth brought about divisions and conflicts among the various groups of the economic classes. WF concerns this social conflicts in workplace. WFs were growing in number at this period. Yet along with this accomplishment we find that there are slight problems as well; surprisingly, there are no, and if any very few, cases of successful evangelization of non-believing co-workers in the company. It seems that the priorities had been shifted. It reminds me, as it is depicted in Acts 6:1-2, of how even those of the early church, after there was a great revival and masses became believers, found themselves in a situation where they were struggling with disunity in regards to relief work, as opposed to clinging harder to the most important things, that is, prayer and the Word: Now during those days, when the disciples were increasing in number, the Hellenists complained against the Hebrews because their widows were being neglected in the daily distribution of food. And the twelve called together the whole community of the disciples and said, 'It is not right that we should neglect the word of God in order to wait on tables.(Acts 6:1-2) Similarly we can see in this period that WFs put more emphasis on the derivative elements rather than on the most important, which was the saving of souls in the workplace. In addition, I would like to point out that much of missions of WF in the workplace was accomplished under the lay leadership, meaning that there decreased a feeling of necessity of the existence of the ordained ministry for the workplace and of the connection between WFs and local churches. Being a time of many shortcomings, this period was also a time during which companies of the faith were founded, and in which lay leadership in ministry is awakened and flourished. I would call this period as 'the Miracle of WF.' V. The Present Stage of the Workplace Faith Fellowship (1991-present) A. Worship Centered Workplace Faith Fellowship On October 12, 2003, the staff workers of True Love Haven Fire Kiln Sauna, Sung Joon Jung and his family, and employees at the Jung Gun Public Company gathered for their first worship service together. They held their Inaugural Worship service on May 23, 2004, with Methodist District Superintendent Haang Sub Jin giving a sermon entitled 'A Desired Church.' The first regular worship service, its format taking after a conventional Sunday service, took place on October 12 with 20 people in attendance. Though similar in form of worship, workplace mission is the focus and priority in this group. Their objective is to help workers lead an upright spiritual life and to encourage workers approach their profession and tasks at the workplace with a 'Christian honesty.' B. Bible Study Centered Workplace Faith Fellowship New Life Training Center ('NLTC') is at the core of a movement representing this type of WF in the period. Purpose of NLTC is Carrying out training programs for mission and raising up disciples in all socio-economic classes; providing helpful resources and strategies to carry out any related ministries; mobilizing believers through a standardized, simple, and easily transmitted methodologies Contents of NLTC Training is as follow: maturing of individual spiritual life; skills for basic ministerial work; expansion of vision; relationship with local church; fulfillment of great commission. The training is composed of four steps of preaching Gospel, nurturing, training, and sending forth. Educational objecitves are as follow: discernable individual spiritual growth; maturing of character with that of spiritual disciplines (QT, Bible studies, prayer); developing of various ministerial skills; deepening ownership of the vision for the spreading of Gospel in each region, in each class, and ultimately all over the world; developing of leadership. C. Mission Centered Workplace Faith Fellowship 1. Korean Christian Bureaucrat Missions Association The Korean Christian Bureaucrat Missions Association was established on November 14, 1998 (General Government Building 19th floor) with 625 members in attendance. The purpose for the founding of this organization lies in their desire to spread the Gospel and Christian spirituality in the realm of public office. Main activities are as follow: formation of mission society in the level of city and providence (March-Oct of 1999); formulating workplace missions strategy and providing a seminar for that (11/27/1999); Christian government employees's mountain prayer meeting for national unity (10/15/1999) Especially concern was laid on structuring of mission strategies, discipleship training system and application strategy with vision to train workplace missionaries. 2. Workplace Faith Fellowship of The Department of Financial Administration and Economy WF of the Department of Financial Administration and Economy had its beginning in December 23, 1994 with the appointment of pastor Gwan Young Kim as Senior Pastor, and Hong Gi Kim as its president in March 3, 1998. The leadership of the group is divided into the president and manager, treasurer, and praise team. Their regular Thursday Bible Study meetings (12-1pm) are held in Language Room 1 of Ahn Nae Dong basement, and their Wednesday Worship Services (12-1pm) and Friday Prayer Meetings (8-gam) in 1-Dong Room 105 in the basement. Membership status are as follows: 11 in the main department, 11 for Tax and Customs Office, 1 from Department of Economic Policy, 1 from the Treasury Bureau, 3 from the World Bank Department, 3 from Department of Economic Cooperation, 1 from the Welfare & Price Policy Bureau, and 12 from the International Court. The group held the 2nd Annual Christian Forum at Gwa Chun government facility on March 23, 2000, and decided to provide financial support on monthly basis for the missions in and abroad and for the Korean Food for the Hungry International, Bethel House, a welfare facility for the disabled, Open Mission Society established for the evangelization of farming communities, and Cross Mission Society founded for teaching Gospel to the disabled, children, and to the aged). In addition, they pray daily for the evangelization of the Ministry of Finance and Economy, the spiritual maturity in members of WF, Christianization of the international economic structure. D. Fellowship-Diakonia Centered Workplace Faith Fellowship 1. Workplace Faith Fellowship of National Correctional Facility WF of National Correctional Facility is community of the people who were called into the unique, and not easily accessible, ministry that gathered to form the National Correctional Facility Christian Fellowship. Like the disciples who were called in the most unlikely of places--under a fig tree, at the tax office, at the beach of Galilee, it is their belief that they, too, have been called forth as heralds of light. Stirred by the Lord's words, ''I was in prison and you came to visit me.''(Mt. 25:36), those from different facilities who received God's holy command gathered voluntarily to organize this fellowship. This WF is named as Correctional Punishment Region Assembly. Christian correction officers from all over the country (43 correctional facilities and jails), with a united vision to establish a union for the sake of spreading the Gospel, began networking since January of 1992, coming to its fruition when 1,500 Christian correction officers from all different correction facilities in the country gathered to offer the Inaugural Founding Worship Service of the National Correctional Facility Christian Fellowship in October 3, 1992 at the Yang Jae Torch Light Missions Center. WF of National Correctional Facility supports the activities of nationally scattered fellowships of 43 (at the present 99) correctional facilities. Modeling after the early apostolic church, this WF is taking on the task of being witnesses to Christ. Furthermore they are concentrating a unified effort to spread the Gospel to the 60,000 inmates, 12,000 correction officers, and 5,000 security officers in the nation. Main activities are as follow: missions Worship Tour to promote spiritual awakening among inmate; charity concert for the evangelizing of prisons; holding training programs for Christian correction officers as well as seminars for those in this particular ministry. With God's calling through the verse ''I was in prison and you came to visit me.'' (Matthews 25:36), 2,000 correction officers take pride in the fact that they are missionaries at the edge, quietly carry on their task to serve wherever they are, and are putting in all their devotion to show that God's kingdom expands even into the prison cells. E. Evaluation 1. Sociological and Theological Evaluation Korea in the 1990s used the authoritarian model of development and experienced an unrivaled growth rate which placed it on 11th place in the world as a powerful international trading country, and in 1995 the country entered into the age of 1 million dollar GNP (at the time it was 9,000,000 won), allowing them to become an OECD member in 1996, which all in turn, made this member of the Four Asian Dragons a subject of research as a model of 3rd world development. Yet on January 23, 1997, the bankruptcy of Han-Bo Steel Company and the downfall of foreign credit rating marked the beginning of a chain of events such as an insolvency postponement agreement, peace talks, court receivership, continued falling of stock and rising exchange rates, and the depletion of usable foreign currency reserves of the Korean bank, led to an official request to the IMF for a rescue loan on December 3, 1997, and as a result of the financial panic after the completion of the rescue loan agreement with the IMF, the economy recession worsened, leaving the country overall in a dire economic crisis. Yet despite the turbulence of going from one economic extreme to another, the National Christian Workplace Mission Council of the 90s, by continuing its organizational expansion into 31 regions to successfully form a national structure, showed a certain systemized strength. In fact, as the members of WFs played their part during the national crisis, the group showed its potential. In this crisis, theological implication of stewardship has played an important role to shape WF's self identity. 2. Overall Evaluation The Korean WFs of this period can be described with 'diversity,' in form as well as in workplaces in which they are founded. From the beginning of the late 90s, responding to what could fairly be termed as a new craze for workplace missions, new mission societies have been formed. The representative organization is the 'Korean Christian Workplace Mission Clergy Association ('KWC').' This association was founded on September 28, 1998 by the ministers of this country's mainstream denominations. KWC and 'Korean Christian Workplace Mission Association,' sharing the same office, expressing their cooperation for mission, still have fundamental differences in the makeup one is for pastors, and the other for laity. The forming of the KWC suggests in some way that the clergy are actively entering into workplace missions. Another problem is the inferior research situation. There is a lack of interest among churches, denominations, seminaries and ministers in this field, not to mention research. This situation is reflected on the publication of books on this subject. Hong-Il Park's book, Workplace Missions and Site of Life was published on February of 2000, and Theology of Mission in Workplace,' authored by Kyung Won Kim, Dong Yoon Jun, and Sang Gi Jun, was published as late as September of 2001. Needless to say, there is an extreme lack of dissertations and research work as well as educational material written on this topic. Within the church, too, education provided for workers is not readily available, not continuous, or systematized. Yet devotion and effort shown by the various WFs deserve acknowledgement and compliments. It is my analysis that these WFs provided great encouragement to Korean workers and Korean citizens overall who were suffering under unprecedented national hardship during IMF period. VI. Conclusion Questions driving the writer last ten year in his double ministries both in the local church and workplace setting are like these: 'Why am I so eagerly involved in the ministry for the workplace along with the ministry for local church?'; 'How could the 'AT help members living faithfully their Christian life in the real life of the workplace?' The writer has revealed, analyzed and evaluated the activities and influence of the WF in four typologies following three stages of historical development with sociological and theological perspective in view. And the thesis intends to be an answer to those questions. One of recent statistics shows that many of workers aged twenty to thirty supposed to be dressed up with excitement and vision, however, feel unsecured in their workplace owing to the threatening situation of economic depression in the larger context and discharge in the small context. It is a symbolic indication of the hard reality of life condition to get through in Korea. Workplace is the one in which the secular and Christian faith is clashed, Christian faith is supposed to take reality, and, the meaning of faith continued to be questioned and deepened in concrete way. WF is the community gathered in the name of Jesus Christ right in this heart of secular section, based on the biblical phrase: 'Where two or three are gathered in my name, I am there among them' (Mt. 18:20), thereby witnessing Lord's presence and its salvafic implications for the people's lives in the workplace. It has been the place in which workers of Christian faith is given hope, encouragement and calling experience. Especially calling experience such that God works through me in this place or God brought me here appears to be the background of ethical and spiritual reading of secular vocation and workplace. It has been the place in which all the Christian members are brought and transfigured into one body of Christ, sharing brotherhood and sisterhood, and, breaking sorrow and joy of life together. Study characterizes WF as a source of spiritual power to help members overcoming duality of faith and life, family and workplace, worship and secular vocation to the maturity of more comprehensive Christian life, defining those effects an important contribution WF made for the Korean church and society. Thesis characterizes activities of WF in four typologies of the worship-centered, the Bible study-centered, mission-centered, and fellowship-centered, and, evaluates each typology from theological and sociological dimension with historical background in view. In chapter II, the writer presents theoretical ground of WF in terms of its historical, theological, and, sociological aspect. Historically, three types of WF were introduced. They are categorized by the nature of leadership: 'Independent WF,' the first Christian meeting held in workplace, 'Workplace Mission Association,' and 'Work Place Church Worship.' Theologically the self identity and activities of these groups in the early stage reflect theology of laity nurtured by the doctrine of priesthood of believers, devotional stewardship, and missiological vision Jesus exemplified in his training and sending of disciples. Sociologically, the writer shows how theses groups adapt themselves in the rapid societal change during 25 years of 'The Five Year Economic Development Plan' designed and led by government. In chapter III, the writer deals with the period beginning from the time of establishment of 'Korean WF' ending up to 1980 when the sequence of several '5 Year Economic Development Project' was closed. Groups are categorized in four and evaluated in its theological and sociological aspect: Worship Centered WF (Congressman's Breakfast Prayer Meeting-1965, Congress Prayer Meeting-1976) Bible Study Centered WF (Korean Bank Mission-1975) Mission Centered WF (Seoul Bank Mission-1977) Fellowship and Social Service Centered WF (Stock Committee Mission-1977). It is evident that groups of this period especially refer to theology of sending for their self identity. In chapter IV, the writer presents several groups belonging to the middle stage covering from 1980 to 1990. WFs in Korea reaches its golden age with the emergence of 'Christian Work Place Mission Council.' Groups are categorized in four and evaluated in its theological and sociological aspect: Worship Centered WF (Sacred Love Church Furniture-1984, Ebenesel WF-1984, Seoul Metropolitan Subway Co. WF-1984), Bible Study Centered WF ('BBB' meaning Business Bible Belt), Mission Centered WF which shows new pattern of workplace mission (City of Incheon WF Association-1988, City of Yeosou WF Association-1984, City of Daegu and Kyoungbuk WF Association-1990, City of Chuncheon WF Association-1990, City of Ulgin Nuclear Power Station WF-1985), Fellowship and Social Service Centered WF (Korean Electronic Co. WF-1989, Korean Drivers' Association-1985). Their activities appears to be grounded upon the theology of laity. In chapter V, the writer presents relatively recent activities of WF. After several decades of individual or corporative activities of WF, there established a 'Korean WF Mission General Council' for more mutual encouragement, exchange of information, and effective mission task. It was remarkable event in the history of workplace mission in Korea. Furthermore this insitution was registered as a corporation aggregate in the Ministry of Culture & Tourism. Groups are categorized in four and evaluated in its theological and sociological aspect: Worship Centered WF (True Love Shelter-2003), Bible Study Centered WFs which use Bible study text produced by NLTC (New Life Training Camp), Mission Centered WF (Korean Government Employee WF Association-1998, Ministry of Finance and Economy WF Association-1994), and, Fellowship and Social Service Centered WF (Korean Correctional Institution WF Association-1992). Their activities appears to be grounded upon the theology of stewardship. The writer attempts to introduce the hidden activities and stories of WF which has exercised positive influence on all sides of lives of Christian families, churches in Korea and of Korean society. They worked voluntarily with resolution. They lighted a candle of love in the darkness of workplace where competition, conspiracy, and hatred predominates, and, proclaimed the Sacred in the cement buildings of modern secular cities. To reveal their devotion, activities and theology itself would be a contribution to Korean churches in general. Churches always emphasize living worship, but not provides structures and leadership for living worship. All kinds of WF function to bridge church and life. Study attempts to cover all kinds of WF activities in full scale. But it was not easy to get all the official informations from WF. WF did not have an office to store the documents nor payed administrative leadership. Making and storing documents were not their primary concern. There might be still so many groups in workplace whose activities are not captured within writer's view. That might be the limit of the study. But if there is still something consoling the writer, it is the fact that there has been not one attempt to categorize WF movement periodically and typologically and to evaluate it with historical, theological, and sociological perspective.
author: 이성원

title: A usability study of users' perceptions toward a multimedia computer‐assisted learning tool for neuroanatomy
abstract:
Abstract

This usability study evaluated users' perceptions of a multimedia prototype for a new e‐learning tool: Anatomy of the Central Nervous System: A Multimedia Course. Usability testing is a collection of formative evaluation methods that inform the developmental design of e‐learning tools to maximize user acceptance, satisfaction, and adoption. Sixty‐two study participants piloted the prototype and completed a usability questionnaire designed to measure two usability properties: program need and program applicability. Statistical analyses were used to test the hypothesis that the multimedia prototype was well designed and highly usable, it was perceived as: (1) highly needed across a spectrum of educational contexts, (2) highly applicable in supporting the pedagogical processes of teaching and learning neuroanatomy, and (3) was highly usable by all types of users. Three independent variables represented user differences: level of expertise (faculty vs. student), age, and gender. Analysis of the results supports the research hypotheses that the prototype was designed well for different types of users in various educational contexts and for supporting the pedagogy of neuroanatomy. In addition, the results suggest that the multimedia program will be most useful as a neuroanatomy review tool for health‐professions students preparing for licensing or board exams. This study demonstrates the importance of integrating quality properties of usability with principles of human learning during the instructional design process for multimedia products.
